headline: High-risk shared-filesystem and MCP pairing: Continue can read/write workspace files while AutoGPT can execute shell and use filesystem, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Continue reads workspace files and can use MCP; AutoGPT can execute shell and access the filesystem. That creates a plausible default bridge where AutoGPT-generated or user-controlled file content can be treated as instructions by Continue. The shared filesystem path is documented, but no provenance tracking is shown, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF AutoGPT writes instruction-like content into a workspace file that Continue later reads
IF Continue is configured to ingest workspace files or MCP outputs as trusted context
mitigations: Restrict both agents to separate workspaces
Disable MCP tools for Continue unless needed
Require manual review of any file-based prompts before Continue reads them
Use read-only mounts for shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between file producers and consumers

B_data_leakage.rationale: Continue explicitly reads workspace files and handles open editor buffers; AutoGPT has filesystem access and allowlisted egress. Even though neither profile shows PHI or secrets handling beyond model keys, shared workspace access means sensitive local code or notes could flow from one agent to the other and out through AutoGPT's network path. This is a default-configurable leakage pathway.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in the shared workspace
IF AutoGPT forwards file contents to an external model or API
mitigations: Separate sensitive and non-sensitive workspaces
Disable network egress for AutoGPT on sensitive projects
Limit Continue to specific folders only
Rotate or redact secrets before either agent reads files
requires-engineering: enforce per-file data classification gates

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write or mutate the same filesystem surface: AutoGPT has filesystem access and shell execution, while Continue can write workspace files and shares state via filesystem across instances. The overlap is enough for concurrent clobbering or inconsistent edits in default use, and no locking is documented. Uncertainty about exact locking means the safer high severity is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same workspace directory
IF either agent writes files without external locking
mitigations: Run the agents in separate directories
Serialize write access with a simple operator-managed lock file
Disable one agent's write access during the other's run
Use version control commits between turns
requires-engineering: add transactional workspace locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Continue can consume workspace files and MCP outputs, while AutoGPT can generate and modify files via shell and filesystem access. If Continue treats AutoGPT-produced artifacts as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream code or actions. Because the pairwise interaction is undocumented and both can act on shared artifacts, the safer high rating is appropriate.
conditions: IF Continue uses AutoGPT-produced files as source-of-truth inputs
IF either agent acts on generated code or plans without verification
mitigations: Require human review before executing generated artifacts
Add a verification step that diffs outputs against source inputs
Keep AutoGPT outputs in a staging folder only
Disable automatic execution of generated scripts
requires-engineering: implement signed handoff between agents

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent, and both are open-source. However, Continue handles editor buffers and workspace files while AutoGPT can access files and egress to allowlisted endpoints, so compliance risk exists if regulated data is placed in the shared workspace. The other agent is not cited for a specific mismatch because none is documented.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the shared workspace
IF AutoGPT sends that data to an external service
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace
Use local-only models for sensitive projects
Review retention settings for any external provider
Document a data-handling policy for the pair
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls
